title: Bud Wilkinson's Hiring at OU and His 145-29-4 Career Record
question: When did Bud Wilkinson become Oklahoma's head coach and what was his overall record?
answer: Bud Wilkinson became Oklahoma's head coach and athletic director in 1947, at age 31, after one season as Jim Tatum's assistant. In 17 seasons through 1963 he went 145-29-4, an .826 winning percentage, and won conference titles in 14 of them.
summary: Bud Wilkinson took over OU in 1947 at age 31 and went 145-29-4 over 17 seasons, winning league titles in 14 of them. Here is how the hire happened.
body: Oklahoma did not have to look far for its greatest early hire. Bud Wilkinson joined Jim Tatum's staff in 1946, and when Tatum left for Maryland after one season, the university handed the 31-year-old assistant both the head coaching job and the athletic director's office for 1947.

Wilkinson was born in Minneapolis and played guard and quarterback for Bernie Bierman at Minnesota from 1934 to 1936. He also held a master's degree in English, and he stressed academics in Norman, where close to 90 percent of his players earned degrees, according to the College Football Hall of Fame.

The results were staggering. Over 17 seasons, from 1947 to 1963, his Sooners went 145-29-4 for an .826 winning percentage. They won conference championships in 14 of those 17 years, and from 1948 through 1958 they went 107-8-2. Along with the famous 47-game streak, his teams also strung together 31 straight wins that ended against Kentucky in the Sugar Bowl after the 1950 season. He was named Coach of the Year in 1949.

Wilkinson stepped down after the 1963 season and later spent years as a national college football TV analyst for ABC. The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 1969, and his 145 wins still rank third in OU history behind only Bob Stoops and Barry Switzer.
